result.summary: This PR implements BIP-348 (OP_CHECKSIGFROMSTACK) as a regtest-only softfork, adding a new tapscript opcode that verifies a Schnorr signature against an arbitrary message and pubkey taken from the stack. It touches the script interpreter, consensus deployment machinery, policy flags, RPC deployment reporting, and adds substantial test coverage (feature_taproot.py, tx_valid/invalid vectors, transaction_tests). The author states there is no effective mainnet policy change since flags currently produce OP_SUCCESS-like behavior, and explicitly says it is meant to be composable with other opcode proposals (e.g. CTV, PR #31989) for a future bundled deployment.
result.problem: Covenant-style proposals (CTV, CSFS, CAT) need a way to be tested and iterated on before any activation decision, and reviewers/implementers need working regtest code to evaluate BIP-348 semantics concretely rather than in the abstract.

result.card: This PR implements BIP-348 (OP_CHECKSIGFROMSTACK) as a regtest-only consensus change, adding the opcode to the tapscript interpreter along with a new BIP9 deployment, policy flag, and substantial test vectors. It solves the problem of covenant-proposal implementers and reviewers needing working code to evaluate the opcode's semantics before any mainnet activation decision, and the author explicitly frames it as composable with other opcode proposals like CTV (#31989) for a future joint deployment. The strongest evidence of importance is that it directly conflicts with six other open, related consensus PRs (CTV, CAT, sighash-cache, annex-discourage, flag-widening), placing it at a live decision point for the covenant-opcode design space. Review state is Stale: the author has been silent for over 490 days, the branch needs rebase, and an unanswered scope question (why tapscript-only) from 1440000bytes remains open. Prior substantive review from JeremyRubin was resolved with a code-review ACK, and several contributors gave concept ACKs with no stated objections.
